info.description:
This course provides a comprehensive understanding of the evolution, transformation, and future directions of the Hospitality and Tourism industries. It highlights the interconnectedness between traditional issues—such as overtourism, crisis management, destination recovery, and the sharing economy—and emerging innovations driven by Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data, and sustainable practices.

Students will explore how these forces collectively shape management, marketing, and service delivery, as well as their ethical and social implications. Key themes include environmental sustainability, digital transformation, AI in guest experience design, and data-driven decision-making.

Throughout the course, students will engage with AI-based platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Perplexity AI, Excel Copilot, and Beautiful.ai) to conduct research, analyse data, and present findings through interactive formats. The course emphasizes experiential learning, collaboration, and critical reflection, helping students bridge theory and practice to develop adaptive and future-ready competencies in the global hospitality landscape.

assessments.knowledgeSkill:
The presentation must cover a specific aspect of the topic mentioned and demonstrate the integration of AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Canva AI, Gemini, Copilot, etc.) to support content creation, data analysis, visualization, or idea development.

Option 2 (For Constructivism Approach only):
Follow lecturer's proposal, encouraging students to apply AI-assisted exploration and reflection as part of their constructivist learning process.
assessments.gradingGuide:
Option 1:
For each topic, each group (4–6 students) will choose an aspect to introduce in different forms such as presentation, case study, workshop, discussion, quiz, games (crossword puzzles, Q&A..), role play... to convey knowledge to other groups in the class.
Students are encouraged to integrate AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Canva AI, Gemini, Copilot, or other generative AI applications) to support research, idea generation, content creation, visual design, data visualization, or simulation activities during preparation and presentation.
With controversial topics, teams can conduct a 1–1 debate on an issue, optionally using AI to simulate arguments, gather contrasting perspectives, or analyze bias.

Each topic lasts 3–4 slots:

Slot 1: General understanding of topics and topic selection by groups.

Slot 2: Groups work, discuss, and use AI tools for research and content development.

Slots 3–4: Group presentations and peer learning.

Scoring recommended (see evaluation forms):

50% by lecturer (50% group, 50% individual)

50% by other groups

Option 2 (For Constructivism Approach only):
Follow lecturer's proposal, with an emphasis on AI-assisted exploration and reflection, where students co-construct knowledge using digital and AI-supported inquiry tools.

assessments.gradingGuide:
The final exam accounts for 30% of the total grade, consisting of multiple-choice questions that assess students’ comprehensive understanding of all course topics.
It covers both traditional issues (overtourism, crisis management, recovery, sharing economy) and emerging trends (AI, Big Data, sustainability, innovation, and digital transformation) shaping the future of the hospitality and tourism industry.
